History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
29-year-old woman with 2-month history of escalating work-related anxiety, insomnia, palpitations, and low mood; referred for talking therapy and basic blood tests, with safety-netting advice.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Progressive anxiety over the last ≈2 months, worst in the mornings before work.  
• Onset/trigger: Coincides with starting new job in a fashion-retail head-office; reports hostile supervisor and high workload.  
• Course: Gradually worsening; fears it may culminate in inability to attend work.  
• Symptoms:
  – Dread/leaving house difficulty each morning.  
  – Palpitations: irregular, rapid heartbeat lasting 2–10 min, mainly on wakening or when fearing lateness; no associated crushing chest pain but describes discomfort while heart racing.  
  – Sleep: Difficulty initiating sleep (bed 22:00–23:00, sleep latency “hours”); shallow sleep; total ≈3–4 h/night; early waking with racing heart.  
  – Low daytime energy, anhedonia; reduced participation in running/tennis and social activities; avoids friends.  
  – Mood: Persistent low mood; no suicidal ideation or self-harm.  
  – Appetite: Largely unchanged; increased chocolate intake.  
  – No prior similar episodes; no panic attacks to date.  
• Exacerbating factors: Thoughts of work, public transport (crowded, hot tube trains).  
• Relieving factors: None reported.  
• Systems review: No weight change, no significant chest pain, no other systemic symptoms mentioned.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.

Medications:
• None currently reported.
• Allergies: Not documented (missing).

Social History:
• Lives with parents at 64 Cliveden Place, South Wimbledon.  
• Occupation: Head-office role for fashion retailer; new sector; high stress.  
• Alcohol: Exceeds recommended limits most Fridays/Saturdays while socialising; occasional glass of wine on weekdays. Exact units not tracked.  
• Tobacco: Occasional smoking.  
• Illicit drugs: Denies.  
• Support: Good family support; mother has history of depression.

Family History:
• Mother – past depression.  
• No other family history reported.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed/not recorded in transcript.

Investigations:
• Planned: “Couple of basic blood tests” (specific panels not detailed) to rule out organic causes of palpitations/anxiety.  
• No prior results available.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Work-related anxiety / probable generalized anxiety disorder
  – Plan:
    • Provide NHS IAPT self-referral link for 1:1 talking therapy (CBT-based).  
    • Recommend reputable online CBT/mental-health resources (details to be messaged).  
    • Offer safety-netting: Return if symptoms worsen, functional impairment increases, or therapy wait unacceptable.  
    • Consider pharmacotherapy (e.g., SSRI) if inadequate response to psychological measures – deferred for now.

Issue 2: Insomnia secondary to anxiety
  – Plan:
    • Supply written sleep-hygiene advice.  
    • Address underlying anxiety as above.

Issue 3: Palpitations
  – Assessment: Likely anxiety-related; organic causes to be excluded.  
  – Plan:
    • Arrange baseline blood tests (e.g., FBC, TFTs, electrolytes, glucose) – patient to book via support line.  
    • GP follow-up one week after results to review and consider further cardiac work-up if indicated.

General Plan items:
• Encourage graded return to exercise (running/tennis) as tolerated.  
• Advise monitoring alcohol intake; counselling on safe limits.  
• Discuss smoking reduction/cessation resources.  
• Provide written summary via patient portal.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Allergies, complete medication list, vitals, mental-state exam, physical exam findings.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear, minimal background noise; no inaudible sections.
